title.narrative: Enhancing Education and Shelter for Vulnerable Communities in Meidaa and Shafuniyeh through Integrated Resilience and Recovery approach

description.narrative: ltpgtSIF aims to address both the immediate critical needs and long-term resilience of vulnerable communities in the Duma sub-district of Rural Damascus, specifically targeting the underserved areas of Meidaa and Shafuniyeh. This integrated and complementary approach is designed to maximize impact and minimize operational costs by targeting 2,506 beneficiaries through a multisectoral strategy based on assessed needs.ltbrgtSIF will enhance its ongoing intervention in Meidaa, where it is currently rehabilitating 50 damaged houses in collaboration with UNHCR. The project will extend support to an additional 34 houses, ensuring that 200 people in need (PiN) have habitable living conditions conducive to sustainable recovery. ltbrgtThe sole secondary school in Meidaa, currently requiring substantial rehabilitation and equipment, will be restored. This intervention is essential to eliminate the financial burden on families whose children currently commute to Adra for education, and to avoid girls being deprived of education due to caregivers' concerns about security risks associated with sending them to another community. This will provide a stable learning environment for 350 students in grades 10 to 12. SIF's education and protection team will provide a comprehensive support package, including immediate remedial classes for at-risk students and a BTL campaign targeting OOSC. This initiative will include NFE activities, aiding in the reintegration of OOSC and facilitating their transition to formal education. To ensure sustainable impact, SIF will train a number of teachers, thereby enhancing the quality of education. The project will also promote child well-being and community involvement through recreational and life skills programs, alongside the establishment of PTA committees in all functional schools.ltbrgtThroughout the project, protection mainstreaming will be a priority. This includes providing PSEA and Accountability to Affected Population (AAP) trainings for all staff and disseminating key messages to beneficiaries. The project will establish safe referral pathways for individuals identified with protection risks and implement efficient complaint and feedback mechanisms to ensure accountability and safety.lt/pgtltpgtltigtIn response to force majeure conditions and the evolving political situation in Syria, the project will further expand its scope to address the increasing humanitarian needs driven by the surge in returnee movements in both Meidaa and Shafuniyeh. This shift has led to heightened demand for shelter and education services, requiring an adaptive response to ensure affected families receive sustainable support. As a result, the total number of beneficiaries will increase from 2,506 to 2,803 without duplication.ltbrgtIn the shelter sector, the rising returnee population in Meidaa has increased the demand for adequate housing, with the number of beneficiaries growing from 200 to 435. To meet this need, the project will extend rehabilitation efforts to an additional 29 DHRs, increasing the total from 34 to 59, ensuring more families have access to safe and habitable living conditions that support long-term stability.ltbrgtIn the education sector, the increasing number of returnee children in both Meidaa and Shafuniyeh has placed additional pressure on existing services. The project will expand its intervention to support 300 more children, bringing the total number of education beneficiaries to 1,100. This will include children benefiting from BTL campaigns, remedial classes, and ALP, ensuring their successful reintegration into the education system while avoiding double counting.ltbrgtBy scaling up these interventions, the project will remain responsive to evolving needs while reinforcing community resilience. The expansion will further enhance the project’s overarching objective of stabilizing returnee populations by addressing critical gaps in shelter and education, ensuring sustainable improvements in living conditions.lt/igtltbrgtlt/pgt
